why: OUR LANGUAGES DISAGREE: three names for one RFC-0033 concept. The alignment-agnostic `view`-mode read over a numeric sequence is `CdrReader::read_le_slice::<T>() -> LeSliceView<T>` in Rust, `rclc_cdr_borrow_le_slice_<t>() -> rclc_le_slice_view_<t>_t` in C (rclc/detail/view.h), and `nros::LeSpan<T>` in C++. Rust says READ, C says BORROW, C++ says SPAN; the `view` byte sequence is `read_slice_u8` in Rust and `rclc_cdr_borrow_bytes` in C. This is the verb the `view` mode should settle on -- BORROW reads correctly against `Publisher::loan`'s borrow/release pair (`c:borrow_loaned_message`) and says the lifetime rule out loud, which READ does not. Phase 379 W5. Note also that the Rust type this returns, `LeSliceView`, is NOT re-exported by the `nros` facade at all -- generated code names `nros_core::LeSliceView` directly -- so the `inline` path and the `view` path reach the user through different crates. DELETED 2026-08-27 (phase-379 W5): the `_raw` five (`read_slice_u16_raw`, `read_slice_u32_raw`, `read_slice_u64_raw`, `read_slice_f32_raw`, `read_slice_f64_raw`) are gone from `packages/core/nros-serdes/src/cdr.rs` -- five definitions, the one unit test (`test_read_slice_f32_raw`) and the doc-comment mention in `traits.rs`, which now names `read_le_slice::<f32>`. Zero consumers, re-verified against `packages/`, `examples/` and every `generated/` tree on disk immediately before the edit. Their five ledger rows went with them -- an item that does not exist needs no row -- so this row is where that family's history now lives. The behaviour is still covered: `read_le_slice_roundtrips_through_cdr` for the CDR round trip and the `LeSliceView` f32 test for decoding. NOTHING UPSTREAM CORRESPONDED: none of rclc/rclcpp/rclrs ships a CDR reader at all (`docs/reference/api-surface/*.json` contain no `cdr` item in any language), so the duplicate family was purely internal dedup with no ROS 2 name to align to -- which is also why the survivor is an `extension` and its only open question is the internal READ/BORROW/SPAN verb disagreement above.
